thread:
maya: Quick sync — proposing we move to per-tenant latency budgets that drive automatic fallback thresholds. Thoughts?

andrew: +1 on per-tenant budgets. We need deterministic signal aggregation though, otherwise noisy tenants will flip the fallback too often.

luke: Can you sketch the policy? e.g. 95th p95 vs p99 vs error-rate blend?

maya: Rough idea: each tenant has config: {budget_ms, window_s, failure_weight}. Primary signal = weighted sum of: latency p95, error rate, backlog length. If > threshold, start fast-fail -> route to backup model/quantized variant.

ida: love the idea. Ops concern: what about oscillation when backup is slower under load? We'll be toggling back and forth.

nora: We should add a cooldown + hysteresis. Also require fallback only when capacity headroom < x%.

andrew: Implementation note: runtime already exposes per-request telemetry (queue_time, compute_ms, model_variant). We can add a sliding window aggregator per-tenant in the router. Keep it approximate to avoid perf blowup (exponential decays).

maya: Example config I'm imagining (pseudo):

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "latency_budget_ms": 250,
  "window_seconds": 60,
  "signals": {
    "p95_latency_weight": 0.6,
    "error_rate_weight": 0.3,
    "queue_length_weight": 0.1
  },
  "fallback_chain": ["redwood-quant4", "redwood-small"],
  "cooldown_seconds": 45,
  "min_headroom_pct": 20
}
```

luke: That looks good. Two questions: 1) how do we compute p95 cheaply across many tenants? 2) where do we store these configs?

andrew: For p95: use T-Digest style sketch per-tenant with reservoir cap and merge across worker shards. Alternatively maintain approximate histograms with fixed buckets tuned for our token latencies. Both are doable.

nora: Store configs in ConfigService (existing feature flags store) with revisioning. Router watches changes via CDC. That gives us rollout safety.

ida: For oscillation: suggest multi-stage fallback state: PROBING -> SOFT-FALLBACK -> HARD-FALLBACK. Probe selects 1% traffic to primary for health checks while most goes to fallback. If probe healthy for 3 windows, advance back.

maya: Nice. Also want an opt-in evaluation mode where we mirror traffic to candidate variant (no user-facing) and compute quality delta. If quality delta > threshold, don't fallback.

andrew: Mirror + fallback sounds expensive for heavy tenants; but we can restrict mirror to sample rate or to tenants under 10rps.

luke: Observability: need per-tenant timeline chart (signal, state, recent switch events) in Console. Also alerting hooks for repeated fallbacks.

nora: Ops-bot idea: if tenant triggers fallback > 3x in an hour, automatically open an incident with pre-filled context and assign oncall. ops-bot: created incident INC-1723 for tenant acme-123 (placeholder).

ida: One more edge: clients that pin model versions. If customer pinned to a heavy model, fallback might violate their contract. We should respect pinning and instead auto-escalate to capacity owners (or only allow fallback to compatible variants).

maya: Agreed — policy should check tenant capabilities (pinning, SLA tier) before fallback. For enterprise customers we surface recommendations but require manual approval.

andrew: On the implementation timeline: I can prototype the aggregator + state machine in the router in 2 weeks. Then a config schema + console work in parallel (luke + nora).

luke: I'll own Console mockups and alerting hooks. Will sync with product for UX constraints.

nora: I'll wire up persistent config + feature-flag gating and the oncall integration.

maya: Plan: andrew builds prototype -> demo in 2 weeks -> we iterate on hysteresis/weights/telemetry. Create RFC doc after demo with formal state machine and control knobs.

ida: Quick gotcha to capture for RFC: the fallback decision must be monotonic w.r.t. request context (i.e., a single request shouldn't race different routers and end up in different variants mid-session). Maybe attach state token to session.

andrew: Good call. We can issue sticky session tokens on first switch. Router caches per-session decision TTL=5m.

luke: OK. This thread good. I'll sketch Console panels and add to RFC draft.

maya: Thanks all — capturing notes into a proposal doc. Will ping when RFC draft is ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reaction :eyes: to maya's message
summary: Per-tenant adaptive latency-budget-driven fallback proposal with signals, state machine (PROBING/SOFT/HARD), cooldowns, headroom checks, mirroring options, pinning respect, and console/ops integrations. Prototype timeline 2 weeks.
